overview: Direct Store Delivery Route Optimisation addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in consumer packaged goods operations. The first proof of value uses delivery windows, vehicle capacity and store order volume. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is delivery cost per drop, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: delivery windows, vehicle capacity and store order volume; define delivery cost per drop and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Commercial Director / Supply Chain VP.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
